s: to flow by, drift away, slip away
5902.full: παρα-ρρέω [in LXX: Isa.44:4 (יָבַל), Pro.3:21 * ;] to flow by, drift away, slip away: Heb.2:1.† (AS)

s: to be beside oneself, be deranged
5904.full: παρα-φρονέω (ιαρά, φρήν), [in LXX: Zec.7:11 (סָרַר)* ;] to be beside oneself, be deranged: 2Co.11:23.† (AS)

5905.lxx: in LXX: 1Ki.21:13 (14) (הָלַל hithpo.), and as seel. 2*
5905.full: παρα-φέρω [in LXX: 1Ki.21:13 (14) (הָלַל hithpo.), and as seel. 2* ;] __1. to bring to, set before, esp. of food (Hdt., al.). __2. to take or carry away: with accusative of thing(s), before ἀπό, Mrk.14:36, Luk.22:42; pass., before ὑπό, Ju 12; metaphorically, pass., with dative, Heb.13:9.† (AS)

s: to step aside out of the way for
5906.full: 1. to go aside, make room, give place, retire , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.: π. τινί to give way, yield, submit , (Plato Philosophus), etc.:—; π. τινός to retire from , (Demosthenes Orator) 2. to step aside out of the way for another, as a mark of respect, ὁδοῦ π. πρεσβυτέρῳ (Xenophon Historicus); π. τινί τοῦ βήματος (Aeschines Orator); τῇ πόλει παραχωρῶ τῆς τιμωρίας I leave the task of punishment to the state, (Demosthenes Orator) 3. to concede a thing, with accusative, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

5907.full: 1. to sit constantly beside, attend constantly, be always near , Lat. assidere, with dative, (Euripides) 2. of judges, to be an assessor , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

5909.full: παρ-επί-δημος, -ον (see: ἐπιδημέω), [in LXX: Gen.23:4, Psa.39:12 (תּוֹשָׁב)* ;] sojourning in a strange place; as subst., ὁ π., a sojourner: of Christians, 1Pe.1:1; ξένοι καὶ π., Heb.11:13; πάροικοι καὶ π., 1Pe.2:11 (see Deiss., BS, 149).† (AS)

5911.full: παρηγορία, -ας, ἡ (παρηγορέω, to address, exhort, console) [in LXX: 4Ma.5:12 4Mac 6:1 * ;] __1. an address, exhortation (LXX, ll. with). __2. comfort, consolation: Col.4:11.† (AS)

5914.full: παροξυσμός, -οῦ, ὁ (παροξύνω), [in LXX: Deu.29:28, Jer.32:37 (קֶצֶף)* ;] __1. stimulation, provocation: π. ἀγάπης, Heb.10:14. __2. irritation: Act.15:39.† (AS)

5917.full: παρά-βασις, -εως, ἡ (παραβαίνω), [in LXX: Psa.101:3 (שֵׂט), 4Ki.2:24 A, Wis.14:31, 2Ma.15:10 * ;] __1. a going aside, a deviation (Arist.). __2. In later writers, an overstepping; metaphorically, transgression (Plut., al.) : Rom.4:15 5:14, Heb.2:2 9:15; τ. νόμου, Rom.2:23; ἐν π., 1Ti.2:14; τ. παραβάσεων χάριν, Gal.3:19 SYN.: see: ἁμαρτία (AS)

s: to obey one in authority, be obedient
5919.lxx: in LXX: Dan LXX 7:27 (שְׁמַע), Sir.33:28, I Est.8:94 *
5919.full: πειθαρχέω, -ῶ (πείθομαι, ἀρχή) [in LXX: Dan LXX 7:27 (שְׁמַע), Sir.33:28, I Est.8:94 * ;] to obey one in authority, be obedient: Tit.3:1; with dative, Act.27:21; θεῷ, Act.5:29, 32.† (AS)

5921.full: one who bears a light shield πέλτη); instead of the heavy ὅπλον, a targeteer , Lat. cetratus, (Euripides), etc. The peltasts held a place between the ὁπλῖται and ψιλοί. (ML)

5922.full: of or for mourning, mournful :—;adverb, πενθικῶς ἔχειν τινός to be in mourning for a person, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

5923.full: 1. five years old , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. of Time, lasting five years , (Thucydides):—; neuter adverb πεντάετες, for five years , (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

s: enclitic particle, adding force or positiveness to the word which precedes it
5924.full: πέρ (akin to περί), enclitic particle, adding force or positiveness to the word which precedes it: indeed, by far, etc. In the NT, it is always affixed to the word to which it relates, see: διόπερ, άἐνπερ, εἴπερ, ἐπείπερ, ἐπειδήπερ, ἤπερ, καθάπερ, καίπερ, ἅσπερ, ὥσπερ ὥσ-περ adv., just as, even as: Mat.6:2 20:28, Act.3:17, 1Co.8:5, 1Th.5:3 al.; in protasis, with οὕτως (καί) in apodosis: Mat.12:40, Luk.17:24, Jhn.5:21, Rom.5:19, Gal.4:29, Jas.2:26, al (AS)

5927.full: to shear or clip all round , (Herdotus Historicus); Mid., περικείρεσθαι τρίχας to have one's hair clipt , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

5929.full: to break one thing round or on another , τί τινι (Plutarch); π. τὸν Τίβεριν to divert it, (Plutarch) (ML)

5930.full: περι-μένω [in LXX: Gen.49:18 (קָוָה pi.), Wis.8:12 * ;] to wait for: with acce., Act.1:4.† (AS)

s: split into two branches so as to surround
to part and go different ways
5932.full: 1. to slit and tear off , (Plutarch) 2. Pass., of a river, περισχίζεσθαι τὸν χῶρον to split round a piece of land, i. e. split into two branches so as to surround it, (Herdotus Historicus);—;so, of a stream of men, to part and go different ways , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

5933.full: 1. to wall all round , πλίνθοις Βαβυλῶνα (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. to surround with a wall , so as to beleaguer, (Thucydides) 3. to build round , ὁ περιτετειχισμένος κύκλος (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

5934.full: περι-τρέχω [in LXX: Amo.8:12, Jer.5:1 (שׁוּט pi.) * ;] to run about: with accusative loc., Mrk.6:55.† (AS)

5935.full: 1. moving round, surrounding , with genitive, (Euripides) 2. surrounded by , with dative, (Euripides) 3. round, circular , (Plato Philosophus):—;of bodies, spherical, globular , (Plato Philosophus):—;of style, rounded , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

s: a going round, rotatory motion, circuit, revolution
5936.full: 1. meats carried round , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. a going round, rotatory motion, circuit, revolution , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. 3. the revolving vault of heaven, (Plato Philosophus) 4. metaphorically, ἐν ταῖς περιφοραῖς in society , (Plutarch) (ML)

5937.full: 1. the line round a circular body, a periphery, circumference , (Aristotle Philosopher) 2. the outer surface , (Plutarch) 3. a round body , (Plutarch) from περιφερής (ML)

5942.full: 1. a standing round, a crowd standing round , Lat. corona, (Theophrastus Philosophus), etc. 2. circumstances, a state of affairs , (Polybius Historicus):—;in bad sense, κατὰ τὰς π. in critical times , (Polybius Historicus) 3. outward pomp and circumstance , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

s: any thing made from its wood, a torch of pine-wood
5944.full: 1. the pine , (Iliad by Homer), etc. 2. any thing made from its wood, a torch of pine-wood , [variant datesTragica Adespota 3. a writing-tablet , (Euripides) (ML)

5948.full: πιάζω (cf. MGr. πιάνω; see Kennedy, Sources, 155), Doric and late Att.. for πιέζω in its later senses [in LXX: Sng.2:15 (אָחַז), Sir.23:21 * ;] __1. to lay hold of: Act.3:7 (Theocr.). __2. to take, capture, apprehend: Jhn.7:30, 32 7:44 8:20 10:39 11:57 21:3, 10 Act.12:4, 2Co.11:32, Rev.19:20 (see MM, xx).† (AS)

5950.full: to turn sideways or aside , πλ. πρὸς τοὺς ἀντίους ἀνέμους (i.e. τὴν ναῦν); to beat up against adverse winds, (Lucian): metaphorically, πλ. ἢ φωνὴν ἢ πρᾶξιν to adapt them to circumstances , (Plutarch) (ML)

5952.full: 1. floating , (Odyssey by Homer); πλωτοί swimmers , i. e. fish, [variant datesAnthology Palantina 2. navigable , (Herdotus Historicus) 3. of seasons, fit for navigation , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

5953.full: πλάνος, -ον [in LXX: Job.19:4 (מְשׁוּגָה), Jer.23:32 * ;] __1. wandering. __2. leading astray, deceiving: πνεύματα π., 1Ti.4:1. As subst., ὁ π., a deceiver, impostor: Mat.27:63, 2Co.6:8 6:1-18 2Jn.1:7.† (AS)

5954.full: the oriental plane , Lat. platanus, (Aristophanes Comicus) From πλατύς, because of its broad leaves. (ML)

5955.full: πλέκω [in LXX: Exo.28:14 (עֲבֹת), Isa.28:5 (צְפִירָה)* ;] to plait, twist, weave: Mat.27:29, Mrk.15:17, Jhn.19:2.† (AS)

5957.full: the organ of breathing, the lungs , Lat. pulmo, (Iliad by Homer): mostly in plural, [variant datesTragica Adespota; πνεῦμ᾽ ἀνεὶς ἐκ πλευμόνων (Euripides) (ML)

5958.full: πνίγω [in LXX: 1Ki.16:14-15 (בָּעַת pi.) * ;] to choke: with accusative, Mat.13:7 (WH, mg.); imperfect (coniative), Mat.18:28; of drowning, pass., Mrk.5:13 (cf. ἀπο-, ἐπι-, συν-πνίγω).† (AS)

5960.full: 1. to work in various colours, to broider, work in embroidery , (Euripides); χορὸν ποίκιλλε he wrought a χορός of cunning workmanship , (Iliad by Homer) 2. to embroider a robe, (Pindar), etc. 3. generally, to diversify, vary , (Euripides):—;of style, to embellish , (Pindar):—; to speak as in riddles , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

5961.full: of or for a shepherd , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus): —; ἡ -κή (i.e. τέχνη); (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

5963.full: 1. one of many , Lat. unus e multis, i.e. the smallest, least , (Thucydides), etc.:—; adverb, δευτέρως καὶ πολλοστῶς in a very small degree , (Aristotle Philosopher) 2. of Time, πολλοστῷ χρόνῳ after a very long time , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

5965.full: to be very careful , opposite to ὀλιγωρέω, (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

5970.full: 1. gone over, passed, passable , (Polybius Historicus); καιρὸς π. the season for travelling , (Polybius Historicus) 2. active going, travelling , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

5971.full: πορισμός, -ου, ὁ (πορίζω, to procure), [in LXX: Wis.13:19 14:2 * ;] __1. a providing. __2. a means of gain: 1Ti.6:5-6 (Polyb., al.).† (AS)

5972.full: of or for harlots , π. τέλος the tax paid by brothel-keepers , (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

5976.full: ποίμνη, -ης, ἡ [in LXX: Gen.32:16 (17) (עֵדֶר), Zec.13:7 A * ;] a flock, prop., of sheep: Mat.26:31, Luk.2:8, 1Co.9:7. Metaphorical, of Christ's followers, Jhn.10:16.† (AS)

5977.full: πρᾳότης, πραότης, see: πραΰτης. πραΰτης (Rec. -ότης, exc. Ja, 1Pe, ll. with, where πρᾳύτης), -ητος, ἡ, late form of πραότης, [in LXX: Psa.45:4 90:10 132:1 (עַנְוָה, עֱנוּת, Est.5:1, Sir.6:1-37 * ;] gentleness, meekness: 1Co.4:21, 2Co.10:1, Gal.5:23 6:1, Eph.4:2, Col.3:12 (see Lft., in l), 2Ti_2:25, Tit.3:2, Jas.1:21 3:13, 1Pe.3:15.† SIN.: ἐπιεικία, q.v (AS)

5979.lxx: in LXX (always -ΰς, exc. 2Ma.15:12, -ᾷος, see Thackeray, Gr., 180 f.) for עָנָו, עָנִי
5979.full: πραΰς, -εῖα, -ΰ, and πρᾷος (Or πρᾶος, ν. Bl., § 3, 3), -α, -ον (see LS, Thayer, see word), [in LXX (always -ΰς, exc. 2Ma.15:12, -ᾷος, see Thackeray, Gr., 180 f.) for עָנָו, עָנִי ;] gentle, meek: Mat.5:5 11:29 21:5" (LXX) 1Pe.3:4.† (AS)

5980.lxx: in LXX: Exo.35:34 (יָרָה hi.), Deu.6:7 (שָׁנַן pi.) *
5980.full: προ-βιβάζω causal of προβαίνω, [in LXX: Exo.35:34 (יָרָה hi.), Deu.6:7 (שָׁנַן pi.) * ;] to lead forward, lead on; metaphorically, to induce, incite, urge: Mat.14:8.† (AS)

5982.full: προ-γίνομαι [in LXX: Wis.19:13 אA, 2Ma.14:3 2Mac 15:8 * ;] to happen before: pf. pass. ptcp., Rom.3:25.† (AS)

5984.full: προ-ετοιμάζω [in LXX: Isa.28:24 B, Wis.9:8 * ;] to prepare before: with accusative of thing(s), Rom.9:23 (οἱς for ἅ by attraction), Eph.2:10.† (AS)

5985.full: προ-εῖδον aor. without Pres. in use (see: προοράω), [in LXX: Gen.37:18 (רָאָה), Psa.139:3 (סָכַן hi.) * ;] to foresee: Act.2:31 (προϊδών; WH, προιδών), Gal.3:8.† (AS)

5986.full: προ-κοπή, -ῆς, ἡ (προκόπτω), [in LXX: Sir.51:17, 2Ma.8:8 * ;] progress (prop., on a journey, then generally): Php.1:12, 25, 1Ti.4:15 (condemned by Atticists, see Rutherford, NPhr., 158).† (AS)

5991.full: 1. to speak to one, to address, accost , (Homer), etc.; πρ. ὀνόματί τινα (Demosthenes Orator):—;with double accusative, τί προσείπω ς᾽ ἔπο; (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. to address as so and so, πρ. τινὰ ὡς ἀλλότριον (Plato Philosophus); πρ. τινὰ χαίρειν to bid him greeting , (Euripides) 3. to call so and so, to name , τί νιν προσείπ; (Aeschulus Tragicus); τοῦτο γάρ ς᾽ ἔχω μόνον προσειπεῖν (Sophocles Tragicus); ὅν μοι προσεῖπας πόσιν whom thou didst name my husband, (Euripides) (ML)

s: to attend constantly, continue stedfastly, adhere to, wait on
5993.lxx: in LXX: Num.13:21 (חָזַק hith.), Tob.5:8 א, Da Th Su 1:6*
5993.full: προσ-καρτερέω, -ῶ (καρτερός, strong, stedfast) [in LXX: Num.13:21 (חָזַק hith.), Tob.5:8 א, Da Th Su 1:6* ;] to attend constantly, continue stedfastly, adhere to, wait on: with dative of person(s), Mrk.3:9, Act.8:13 10:7; with dative of thing(s), Act.1:14 2:42 6:4, Rom.12:12, Col.4:2; before ἐν, Act.2:46; εἰς, Rom.13:6.† (AS)

s: to wait longer, continue, remain still
to remain attached to, cleave unto, abide in
5995.lxx: in LXX: Jdg.3:25 A (חוּל hi.), Tob.2:2 א, Wis.3:9, 3Ma.7:17 *
5995.full: προσ-μένω [in LXX: Jdg.3:25 A (חוּל hi.), Tob.2:2 א, Wis.3:9, 3Ma.7:17 * ;] __1. to wait longer, continue, remain still: Act.18:18; before ἐν, 1Ti.1:3. __2. C. dative, to remain with: Mat.15:32, Mrk.8:32. Metaphorical, to remain attached to, cleave unto, abide in: τ. κυρίῳ, Act.11:23 (R, txt.; ἐν τ. κ., R, mg., see supr.); τ. χάριτι τ. θεοῦ, Act.13:43; τ. δεήσεσιν, 1Ti.5:5.† (AS)

5997.full: 1. to play or sport with , τινί (Xenophon Historicus) 2. absolute to sport, jest , (Plato Philosophus) 3. with accusative, πρ. θεούς to sing to the gods, ὕμνον πρ. τὸν Ἔρωτα sang a hymn in praise of Eros, (Plato Philosophus) 4. to banter , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

5998.lxx: in LXX: Psa.92:1-15 title. א (שַׁבָּת) שַׁבָּת) Psa.93:1-5 title., Jdth.8:6 *
5998.full: προ-σάββατον, -ου, τό [in LXX: Psa.92:1-15 title. א (שַׁבָּת) שַׁבָּת) Psa.93:1-5 title., Jdth.8:6 * ;] the day before the Sabbath: Mrk.15:42 (L, Tr., txt., πρὸς σ.).† (AS)
